automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.basis: Strict two-day public-source window relative to run timestamp
cutoff_window.date_policy: Included sources with visible publication or update dates inside the window. Excluded missing, ambiguous, future-dated, stale, duplicate prior-run, and boundary-only dates.

federation_policy.local_scope: Practice-level AI-assisted development implications, operating patterns, governance, verification, workflow, and adoption notes.
federation_policy.handling: Named ecosystem entities are recorded as upstream-owned. Findings include only the downstream practice implication or routing note.

findings.title: AI-generated code volume is outpacing review capacity
findings.summary: Qodo published survey findings from 100 engineering directors and VPs, reporting broad AI coding tool adoption, limited confidence in AI-generated code quality before production, and review bottlenecks among standardized AI-tool teams. Futurum covered the same research as a trust gap between AI code generation speed and production-grade engineering controls.
findings.why_it_matters: AI-assisted development practice needs review capacity, architectural checks, standards enforcement, and quality evidence scaled to AI-generated code volume. Adoption guidance should not treat tool rollout as complete until review infrastructure catches up.
findings.local_practice_implication: Coding-practice and verification pages can later frame AI code review as a capacity and trust system, with manual review, static analysis, and dedicated AI review roles separated explicitly.
findings.routing_note: Route vendor and market-position coverage upstream; keep only review operating-model implications locally.

findings.title: Code-review retrieval shifts from source search to review memory
findings.summary: Qodo described reducing a broad codebase RAG index for code review after measuring low incremental lift against maintenance cost, while keeping retrieval for PR-history memory, repeated feedback, and team-specific decisions that are not recoverable from the working tree.
findings.why_it_matters: Codebase retrieval guidance should distinguish context an agent can rediscover with tools from durable team memory that must be stored. RAG for code review is becoming an economic and measurement decision, not a default architecture.
findings.local_practice_implication: Retrieval pages can later describe a split between on-demand agent navigation over source code and curated memory over review decisions, including cost and quality measurement gates.
findings.routing_note: Keep Qodo product details and broad RAG technique background upstream; local wiki owns the code-review retrieval practice pattern.

findings.title: Persistent memory pattern for code review agents
findings.summary: Mem0 published a practical code review agent architecture using persistent memories for repository history, prior comments, project rules, file metadata, and developer-specific feedback, with the memory layer used during context assembly and result persistence.
findings.why_it_matters: Review agents need explicit memory contracts: what is remembered, how it is tagged, how it is retrieved, and how it stays within token and latency budgets. This supports consistent reviews across pull requests rather than single-diff prompting.
findings.local_practice_implication: Context architecture pages can later define repository, file, team, and reviewer memory dimensions for AI-assisted code review, with retrieval precision and governance caveats.
findings.routing_note: Route Mem0 product details upstream; local wiki owns the memory-for-review workflow pattern.

findings.title: Agent governance guidance emphasizes shadow MCP usage and audit evidence
findings.summary: MintMCP published an agent-governance roadmap for EU AI Act readiness, focusing on AI system inventory, risk classification, shadow AI detection, MCP gateway controls, audit logs, human oversight, credential management, and behavioral drift monitoring.
findings.why_it_matters: Governance guidance for AI-assisted development should account for local developer tools and MCP connections that bypass central visibility. Audit evidence needs to capture who invoked which tool, what data was touched, and what policy was enforced.
findings.local_practice_implication: Governance pages can later add shadow-agent discovery and MCP audit evidence as first-class operating practices, without restating legal or product background.
findings.routing_note: Route EU AI Act background, MintMCP product coverage, and MCP protocol background upstream; keep the downstream governance implication.

findings.title: Vendor-published agent skills package domain integration instructions
findings.summary: Scandit published Agent Skills that teach coding agents to integrate barcode, ID, and label scanning, framing the skills as reusable instructions for AI coding agents rather than only human-facing SDK documentation.
findings.why_it_matters: Durable agent instructions are becoming a distribution format for domain integration knowledge. Practice guidance should distinguish vendor-owned instruction packs from local project rules, and should require review before importing third-party coding-agent behavior.
findings.local_practice_implication: Prompt and instruction pages can later cover third-party skill intake, trust review, version pinning, and local adaptation for domain-specific SDK work.
findings.routing_note: Route Scandit product and SDK details upstream; keep the local practice implication around governed instruction ingestion.

findings.title: Public incident report highlights destructive shell-command risk
findings.summary: A public Cursor community incident report described an AI coding agent running a misquoted Windows recursive deletion command during a Gradle cleanup attempt, causing broad local file deletion risk outside the intended project scope.
findings.why_it_matters: Agent workflow guidance should treat destructive shell commands as a separate risk class with working-directory constraints, command previews, path normalization, backups, and approval gates before execution.
findings.local_practice_implication: Governance and workflow pages can later add concrete guardrails for cleanup commands, quoting-sensitive shell operations, and cross-drive path containment.
findings.routing_note: Route Cursor product details upstream; keep only the destructive-command approval and containment lesson locally.
